$comment: Interaction motion. REPO-OWNED — this file is not a Figma export.
It lives at the package root, beside token-overrides.json and deliberately
OUTSIDE src/figma/, because a re-export overwrites everything in there.
WHY THESE ARE NOT TOKENS
Figma can express motion — it is authored as prototype reactions, readable
at node.reactions[].action.transition — but it is not a variable, so there
is nothing for a token to alias. Same situation as effect styles, same
answer: commit the values and generate CSS from them. The `--ion-` prefix
marks it, exactly as it does for `--ion-shadow-*`: anything named
`--duration-*` would have come from the token pipeline, and none of this
does.
The one prototype interaction in the Figma file (Button, Primary Brand,
Small + Medium) specifies 300ms cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 1, 1). That curve is
Figma's Ease In preset: flat start, arriving at full velocity. It is the
wrong shape for a colour hold and is not reproduced here — see `ease.in`,
which carries the value for the cases it does suit.
A LADDER, NOT A SET OF RECIPES
These are indexed by value and a component picks a rung. There is no
`duration/hover` or `ease/press` and there should not be: that is indexed
by usage, so it needs a new entry per usage pattern. The same reasoning
deleted the control/<size>/* group from Semantics.

fast.use: Press and release. Must resolve before the finger leaves the button, or the feedback reads as lag rather than as a press.

base.use: The default for any state colour change — hover, focus, selection, validation. Replaces a hardcoded 150ms that read as abrupt.

slow.use: Anything that travels or changes size: panels, overlays, disclosure. Distance needs time; a colour does not.

out.use: The default. Leaves immediately and decelerates into the end state, so the change reads as settling. Correct for anything entering a state and staying there.

in.use: Accelerates and arrives at full velocity. Only for things leaving — dismissing an overlay, collapsing a panel. On a state a user is entering it reads as a snap.

in-out.use: Symmetric, for two-way travel where the same element moves back and forth — the Toggle knob. This is the curve every stylesheet used for everything, which is why state changes felt jerky.

linear.use: Continuous progress only, where easing would misreport position. Never for interaction.
